## Dual Special Needs Plans (D-SNP) — Medicare + Medicaid
- **Hub page**: https://medicareenrollmentnevada.com/dual-special-needs-plans-nevada.html
- Nevada operates a **coordination-only D-SNP (CO D-SNP)** program — plans coordinate Medicare and Medicaid rather than fully integrating them (not FIDE-SNP or HIDE-SNP)
- Dual eligibility categories currently enrolled: Full Benefit Dual Eligible (FBDE), Qualified Medicare Beneficiary (QMB), Qualified Medicare Beneficiary Plus (QMB+); the state has moved to expand to SLMB and SLMB+
- **January 1, 2026**: Nevada expanded Medicaid managed care beyond Clark and Washoe counties to all 17 counties, moving roughly 75,000 rural residents from fee-for-service into managed care. CareSource and SilverSummit Healthplan were awarded the rural expansion
- Enrollment: CMS eliminated the quarterly dual/LIS special enrollment period on January 1, 2025. A monthly SEP exists for standalone Part D, and a monthly integrated-care SEP applies only to aligned integrated D-SNPs — which generally does not cover Nevada's coordination-only plans. Nevada duals typically use AEP (Oct 15–Dec 7), MA OEP (Jan 1–Mar 31), or an SEP triggered by a change in Medicaid or Extra Help status

## 2026 plan availability in the 11-county service area
- Rural Nevada has historically had far fewer Medicare Advantage options than Clark and Washoe counties
- For 2026 the number of options across this 11-county service area has expanded, making it worth re-comparing
- Availability is defined county by county and changes each plan year; verify at Medicare.gov or 1-800-MEDICARE

## Nevada Medigap birthday rule
- Nevada is one of a small number of states with a Medigap birthday rule, created by Assembly Bill 250 and codified at NRS 687B.352, effective January 1, 2022
- The window opens on the first day of the policyholder's birth month and remains open for at least 60 days
- Inside the window a current Medigap policyholder may switch to a policy with the same or lesser benefits with no medical underwriting
- It is a switching right for existing Medigap policyholders; it does not apply to someone moving from Medicare Advantage to Medigap
